TASK: The operator was removing a misfed sheet from the laminating press during a size changeover. The task was underway because a sheet had misfed at the end of the previous run and had to be cleared before the changeover could finish. Stage of the task: teardown, changeover or breakdown. Method in effect: SW-508 Laminator Changeover. The task was not being performed as written. The difference from the written method was as follows: the written method requires the platens to cool below 120 degrees Fahrenheit before the press is entered, but the sheet was cleared while the platens were still at running temperature to save about forty minutes of cooling. Equipment involved: Laminating press LP-03, upper heated platen. Equipment state at the time: hot, de-energized and guard, cover or barrier removed. Equipment condition: Normal working order with no open maintenance items. Object handled weighed a laminate sheet of approximately 2 pounds. Object size and shape: about 40 by 30 inches, thin and flexible. The object was held as follows: gripped at the near corner with the right hand, wearing general purpose gloves. PPE in use: Safety glasses and general purpose cotton gloves, not heat resistant. This differed from the PPE specified for the task.

SEQUENCE: Immediately before the event: standing at the front of the press with the guard swung open, right arm extended into the press about 18 inches with the hand on the near corner of the sheet. At the moment of the event: the sheet tore as it was pulled, the right hand travelled forward and the back of the hand contacted the underside of the upper heated platen. Immediately after the event: the hand was withdrawn immediately, the operator stepped back from the press and walked to the sink, and the changeover was stopped.

MECHANISM: Source: The upper heated platen of laminating press LP-03. Magnitude: Approximately 300 degrees Fahrenheit at the platen surface. Contact duration and area: momentary, less than a second, across the back of the right hand. Isolation state: The press was de-energized at the control panel but the platens had not been allowed to cool, and the written method requires cooling below 120 degrees Fahrenheit before entry. Point of contact and direction of force: across the back of the right hand between the knuckles and the wrist, contacting a surface above it as the hand travelled forward.

CONDITIONS: Difference from a normal run of this task: The changeover was being done between shifts rather than at the scheduled slot, so there was no time allowed for the platens to cool. Conditions at the point of injury: hot and time or production pressure. Detail: The area in front of the press runs warm during a changeover and the crew were working to hand the machine over at shift change. Timing: About 7 and a half hours into an 8 hour shift and roughly 15 minutes into the changeover. The operator had performed this task before. A known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. Detail: Heat resistant gloves are specified in the risk assessment for this press but are not stocked at the station. A guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Detail: The front guard was swung open to reach the sheet, and opening it does not prevent access to the platens while they are hot. Stop-work opportunity: The changeover could have been left for the incoming shift once the platens had cooled, but the handover was already late.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: First aid at the scene: The hand was held under cool running water at the sink for about 20 minutes and covered loosely with a sterile dressing. This was self-administered. Notification: The team lead was told within about five minutes and EHS at the end of the shift. Scene and equipment: The press was left open to cool and tagged out of service until EHS attended. Work at the location stopped. The operator was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
